paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Some people in this story spent their time plotting. Some spent their time counting. And one woman just gave. The chief priests wanted a covert way to arrest Jesus (Mark 14:1), and the grumblers did the math on her perfume, "over three hundred denarii" (Mark 14:5). She didn't do math. She broke the jar.

Jesus called it "a beautiful deed to Me" (Mark 14:6). I think that's the part to hold onto. She did "what she could" (Mark 14:8), and Jesus said so Himself. He didn't ask her for a bigger jar or a better plan. He took what she brought and called it beautiful.

So here's what it means for you, baker. Loving Jesus isn't always the efficient choice, and sometimes people will scold you for it, like they scolded her (Mark 14:5). But Jesus noticed her, defended her, and promised her deed would be told "in memory of her" (Mark 14:9). Whatever you bring Him, you bring it to Someone who sees it. And this story is far from over, so keep your ovens ready.
